name: Algonav
description: AlgoNav is a specialist for kinematic high-precision positioning based on the fusion of raw GNSS observations and other sensors, as IMU, odometers, cameras, and laser scanners. The company was established in Darmstadt in May 2024. AlgoNav Rail is the worldwide first cloud-based SaaS for the positioning of rail vehicles, as used for rail infrastructure mapping and regular monitoring tasks. The core positioning engine employs innovative sensor fusion techniques, striving for an unprecedented accuracy and robustness also in very difficult GNSS environments. The project is carried out in cooperation with DB InfraGo AG. The algorithms and cloud platform to be developed will lay out a basis for AlgoNav’s future expansion into other market segments. The platform will allow a very high degree of automation, addressing B2B-customers with large amounts of data, from industries such as rail/urban/industrial infrastructure mapping and monitoring, and geophysical surveying. AlgoNav’s proprietary algorithms have a strong emphasis on raw multi-frequency multi-constellation GNSS processing, both for stand-alone (PPP) and differential approaches. Particular characteristics of Galileo will be addressed and exploited, targeting positioning robustness and accuracy. A tight integration with laser scanner data will further support the GNSS error detection and mitigation.

name: AllSpace
description: AllSpace's mission is to inspire and motivate generations of all age to gain confidence and expertise in operating real space technology, creating a large think tank that brings innovative new ideas into space industry. With the aim of democratizing access to space for education, training, and practical applications, is developing rover platforms. Initially focused on the academic and NewSpace sectors, AllSpace offers fully functional open-source rover systems that can be modified, extended, and operated. The key value of these rover systems is that they are in fact "CubeSats on wheels". They used components are (to large extend) identical with those used for satellites. They use CCSDS/ECSS space communication protocols and space standards for the on-board flight software and external communication. This way, users can train and deploy operations of the rover in the same way as they would for a satellite mission. In essence, the rovers can be operated much like modern ESA satellites, utilizing CFDP file transfer, PUS packet service, PLUTO for automation, and more.

name: Aperio Space
description: Aperio Space Technologies GmbH develops key technologies and software for resilient, secure, and scalable satellite networks with a platform-independent approach. With a patent-pending method for dynamically determining network topology and operating a multi-orbit and multi-platform satellite network, Aperio enables operators to access their satellites in real time to retrieve data and perform continuous operations. After joining the Aperio network, satellites will be able to downlink more data faster, thereby increasing mission returns. This is particularly crucial in earth observation, where the instant availability of large amounts of data is critical for applications such as disaster response, environmental monitoring, infrastructure monitoring, cargo monitoring, and surveillance. Through intelligent dynamic routing, the data traffic in future telecommunication networks that (even partly) rely on satellites will be optimized and secured with advanced cryptographic mechanisms that Aperio integrates into their protocols. At the same time, space will become safer through Aperio’s work. Not only does the dynamic topology eliminate single points of failure and make telecommunication and earth observation constellations much more resilient, but it also enables instant maneuvering for collision avoidance and autonomous operations, which will become mandatory given the exponential rise of active satellites in orbit. name: Astra Labs
description: Safety critical systems require extensive documentation for qualification in space applications like satellites, probes and manned spacecraft. Writing documentation is often more extensive than the development of the system itself as it undergoes multiple iterations and constant change. Especially small and medium enterprises can’t afford to hire dedicated teams to manage a project's documentation for qualification. Even in large enterprises, documentation effort is one of the most significant drivers for project cost. Astra Labs is developing a next generation documentation tool to automate these manual tasks. Our goal is to supercharge the European space industry by reducing cost and time for the development of safety critical spacecraft and ground systems. We utilize novel algorithms and artificial intelligence to generate review-ready documentation that adheres to industry standards. Just review and submit to your customer.
